captures.notes: The compact silhouette is built from fourteen connected narrow/deep stacks. Structural surfaces show the authored light plank meshes; the former dark generated skins are absent.
The reverse overview shows staggered rooflines and supported intermediate floors. No room has an open top and no broad central lawn or raw cavity remains.
The side section confirms complete pitched caps, retained half-level terraces, and multiple public layers crossing one another.
The stocked market establishes the intended lower bazaar, but canopy foreground occupies too much of this verification frame.
The lower reverse route reads as a bounded exterior canyon beneath occupied mass and connected upper galleries. Its adversarial chord is visually blocked.
A second lower-route chord still has an uninterrupted view through the market to the outside horizon. This fails the horizontal maze test despite the corrected vertical coverage.
The public route is connected and guarded, but a lower blue roof crowds the foreground enough that the level relationship needs a tighter alignment review.
Only one third of the required target samples are visible; nearby roofs and facade mass prevent this named view from proving the complete occupied link.
The exterior-air view beneath the selected link is collision-clear and shows inhabited mass above the lower realm without exposing a broad central shaft.
Every visible room, shallow bay, corner overlap, and straight occupied link terminates in a measured pitched roof with sealed ends.
Connected upper galleries now cover lower-route columns and leave only four isolated guarded lightwells plus one uncovered macro column. The former large see-through-to-ground area is absent.
